title: Developing and time-wasting moves

D0.outcome: Explains that a developing move adds to the working power of a piece or opens a line it needs, and a time-wasting move does not.

D1.outcome: In an early opening position, picks the move that develops with most effect and names a move that wastes time (a rook-pawn move, a needless queen move).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled opening positions, chooses between developing and non-developing moves, including positions where a rook-pawn or pawn move is the concrete answer to a threat.

D3.outcome: Predicts how the position's character (a settled structure, a pinned knight) makes a quiet or non-developing move right, and which default it overrides.

misconceptions: Knights before bishops is a law.
Develop fast means make as many different piece moves as possible.
Never move a pawn beyond the centre pawns.
conditions: Nothing concrete forces a different move.
The developed piece stands on a useful line, not merely off the back rank.
contrasts: A useful-looking rook-pawn move adds no force while the opponent has an open line to a weak point.
'knights before bishops' applied as a law where the structure favours the bishop first.
A real pin where a rook-pawn move is the concrete answer.
